items.title: Commencement
notes:
A meeting of City Council was held at 2:00 p.m. this date, chaired by Mayor B. Vrbanovic. Notice of this meeting had been previously given to all members of Council by the City Clerk pursuant to Chapter 25 (Council Procedure) of the Municipal Code.

The meeting began with a Land Acknowledgement given by the Mayor.

items.title: Recess and Reconvene
notes: The Special Council meeting then recessed at 2:03 p.m. and reconvened at 2:16 p.m. in the Conestoga Room, chaired by Mayor B. Vrbanovic, with all members present except Councillor P. Singh.

items.title: Shaping the 2027-2030 Strategic Plan - Synthesizing Inputs and Identifying Key Priorities, CAO-2026-327
notes:
Council considered Chief Administrative Officers report CAO-2026-327, entitled Shaping the 2027-2030 Strategic Plan - Synthesizing Inputs and Identifying Key Priorities, dated August 10, 2026, which highlights a prioritization exercise to receive feedback from Council regarding strategic priorities for the 2027-2030 Council term. 

M. Love provided opening remarks noting the purpose of the session this date is to synthesize feedback previously provided by Council regarding potential strategic priorities and to obtain additional insights to inform the development of the 2027-2030 Strategic Plan.

Councillor P. Singh entered the meeting at this time.

D. Coletto, Founder, Chair and CEO of Abacus Data, provided a presentation outlining insights regarding the factors shaping Kitchener's strategic direction. D. Coletto stated, findings from workshops conducted with Staff regarding operational realities and the City's capacity to deliver services indicate that many organizational pressures are being managed through Staff work that is not readily visible. D. Coletto further advised that multiple independent evidence streams consistently identified a common strategic challenge: maintaining residents' quality of life while strengthening the City's capacity to manage growth, uncertainty, and interconnected pressures.

D. Chapman then provided an overview of key themes arising from individual interviews conducted with Council members which include, providing results driven services, advancing affordability and fiscal discipline, delivering core service excellence, strengthening inclusion and high quality of life and strengthening economic development and downtown vitality. 

K. Rieger advised that, in response to the feedback Council provided at the May 4, 2026, Strategic Session, Staff engaged an additional 550 residents to identify demographic trends behind the survey results previously presented. K. Rieger noted, most demographic groups aligned closely with the citywide survey results reinforcing the potential priority themes identified through the public engagement process.

M. Love then led a prioritization exercise where members of Council were asked to identify themes arising from the survey results which they wish to accelerate, to possibly advance some actions or to maintain the current approach. D. Chapman then provided observations comparing the results of Council's prioritization activity to the results of the resident panel prioritization activity. 

K. Rieger noted, Staff will synthesize the results of the prioritization activities and discussions this date to develop draft strategic priorities and will report back to Council in November 2026.
